text.tspan: The serial connection uses 3 pairs of lines:
• The inner pair (pins 3,4 or AB) is for ScoringBox → Peripheral
• The second pair (pins 2,5 or CD) is for Peripheral → ScoringBox
Peripherals that only receive may omit U2 & R2.
Using ground and 5V requires special care:
• Standard RJ11 cables usually only have the middle 4 wires (pins 2,3,4,5),
and so won't connect to these pins at all.
• Standard RJ14 cables (6P6C) usually SWAP pairs. If you are using one
of these cables, you'll have to expect ground on 6 and 5V on 1.
• "Straight" RJ14 cables will not swap the pins. The problem is that not
swapping AB and CD means that they will be inverted, which can
mess up most UARTs. The RP2040 can invert the UART input to
Also, the 5V is intended only for short cables and low power usage!
It can power a microcontroller, but not indicator lights! Loads of more
than 300mA may be considered a short and power will be cut.
ABTX controls whether AB is transmitting (H) or receiving (L).
For peripherals, ABTX should generally be LOW (receiving from the scoring box).
When ABTX is low, U1 will drive RX.
CDTX controls whether CD is transmitting (H) or receiving (L).
For peripherals, CDTX should be HIGH to transmit commands to the scoring box.
When CDTX is low, U2 will drive RX.
- It is important to have protection from static shocks on the inputs. The
THVD1450DR chip has built-in ESD protection, but if you use a
different chip you should ensure adequate static protection, such as
BAV99 diodes on each line (A, B, C, D).
- The 120Ω resistors between AB and CD is important to reduce reflections
on longer cables. Don't omit them.
This is a full-duplex RS-485 serial communication with limited power supply over a 6P6C modular cable.
